 LIVE UPDATES NBA Portland Trail Blazers vs. Los Angeles Lakers Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
 Zach Buckley Oct 27, 2026, updated 2 min ago 
 Something's gotta give.
 The Los Angeles Lakers and Portland Trail Blazers will both carry unblemished records into Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday night. Only one will make it out with perfection still intact.
 Their early successes have stemmed from similar places. They've had soft schedules, for starters, and their offenses have absolutely feasted on the opposition. The Lakers are following the ludicrous lead of the Luka Dončić-Austin Reaves pairing, while the Blazers are so far balancing the Damian Lillard-Ja Morant backcourt and still finding ways to showcase forwards Deni Avdija and Toumani Camara.
 This could be one of those first-to-get-a-stop-wins games, as both offenses have seemed unstoppable so far. But this is also the best team either has faced, so maybe some of these league-leading numbers will slow down a bit. ( Although, for the record, you can consider us totally down for a sprint to 130 points .)
 It should be an action-packed, aesthetically pleasing evening, and we'll be here throughout with all of the updates, highlights and takeaways you could possibly need.
 Live Updates
 32 Total Posts
 Newest First ​ Just Now 12:31 AM Speaking of Reaves' Playmaking
 Milestone dimes being dropped tonight.
 Just Now 12:30 AM Reaves Is Making Plays, Mamu Is Making Shots
 Luka entered intermission with four assists against a single turnover (oh, and 24 points), and Reaves bettered him on both fronts with five assists and zero giveaways. Sandro Mamukelashvili has his own heater going with 13 points in 11 minutes on 4-of-5 shooting (3-of-3 from range).
 Score: Lakers 73, Blazers 68 | End of the second quarter 
 7 mins ago 12:25 AM Putting the Late in Late Night
 These guards aren't easy to contain, and they seem to all have the gas pedal floored. Make it an even 40 three-throw attempts between the teams so far.
 Score: Lakers 70, Blazers 68 | 0:05 remaining in the second quarter 
 10 mins ago 12:23 AM Bouncy Bigs Are Eating Good Tonight
 Downhill guards with floor vision plus centers with some vertical lift equals a whole lot of bunnies.
 13 mins ago 12:20 AM Troublesome Whistles for the Trail Blazers
 The Blazers haven't even made it to halftime yet, and they already have Toumani Camara sitting with three fouls—and Deni Avdija benched with four. Uh-oh.
 Score: Blazers 65, Lakers 64 | 1:28 remaining in the second quarter 
 17 mins ago 12:16 AM Ja Is Throwing the Ball in an Ocean
 Five field-goal attempts. Five makes. Four free-throw attempts. Four makes. One long-range look after a couple of quick, late-clock passes. One silky splash.
 Score: Lakers 64, Blazers 63 | 2:15 remaining in the second quarter 
 22 mins ago 12:11 AM Ja Morant Looks Like...Ja Morant
 A healthy Morant is almost impossible to stay in front of. This is just ridiculous execution from both of these starting backcourts.
 23 mins ago 12:09 AM Is Walker Kessler a Lock to Lead the League in Field-Goal Shooting?
 Being the rim-running center in a Luka-led offense has obvious perks, but Kessler gets the benefit of having a second high-end creator in the backcourt. Screen, crash, crush, repeat.
 27 mins ago 12:06 AM Can the Backup Big Man Search Start Tonight?
 Kevon Looney is a seasoned pro and the proud owner of a respectable NBA career, but yikes, the difference of the Lakers with Looney vs. when they have Walker Kessler manning the middle is jarring. L.A. is winning Kessler's minutes by three and losing Looney's short run by eight.
 Score: Blazers 58, Lakers 54 | 4:15 remaining in the second quarter  
 31 mins ago 12:02 AM If Portland Wants It, Portland Gets It
 There's probably at least a hint of generosity on behalf of L.A.'s defense, but Portland's offense is putting on a clinic. The Blazers are nearly a quarter-and-a-half through this game and still posting a preposterous 73.9 field-goal percentage. Good gracious.
 Score: Blazers 50, Lakers 48 | 6:37 remaining in the second quarter  
 34 mins ago 11:59 PM Sloppy Start for Scoot
 It feels like everyone is grooving in this game, but Scoot Henderson is the obvious exception. He looks somehow both sped-up and hesitant, a brutal combination that has him really mucking up an otherwise red-hot offense.
 Score: Blazers 49, Lakers 48 | 6:59 remaining in the second quarter  
 38 mins ago 11:55 PM Perfect Start for Portland's Other All-Star Point Guard
 It'd be fascinating to know how the future will regard the price Portland paid for Ja Morant this summer. His trade value was tanked for a reason, but he is such a special talent when he's right.
 Score: Lakers 46, Blazers 42 | 9:00 remaining in the second quarter 
 42 mins ago 11:50 PM Defense Optional Kind of Night
 It's just relentless attacking at both ends. The stat pages say these are the NBA's two best offenses, and the eye test is clearly and convincingly saying the same.
 45 mins ago 11:48 PM All Gas, No Brakes
 It just feels full-throttle at all times for both teams. If there's even a hint of an opening, someone is getting downhill and hitting it hard.
 Score: Lakers 38, Blazers 32 | End of the first quarter 
 47 mins ago 11:46 PM Ziaire's Delectable Dime
 The slashing wing goes behind-the-back to feed the dynamic playmaker? Everything is possible in the modern NBA, and I am very much here for it.
 49 mins ago 11:44 PM Bench Energy Boosts Both Ways
 If I'm going to spotlight Portland's second-teamers, I better do the same for L.A.'s. This game is being played at a blistering pace, and the action hasn't slowed up a second since reserves started hitting the hardwood.
 50 mins ago 11:43 PM Luka Cooking Up Another Monster?
 The Trail Blazers have some really high-end defenders, and they're throwing some of their best at Luka (Toumani Camara to start, now Jrue Holiday). It just hasn't mattered. The current scoring leader is looking the part with 16 points already.
 Score: Lakers 36, Blazers 29 | 1:22 remaining in the first quarter 
 53 mins ago 11:40 PM Empowering Multiple Playmakers
 You know what those "there's only one ball!" concerns overlook? The fact that having multiple offensive triggers can unlock some really good second and third actions in the offense. I do not envy the defenders in this game.
 58 mins ago 11:35 PM Blazers' Bench Matching the Surge
 It's been a mostly electric start for the Lakers, but the Blazers are finding plenty of jolts of their own. Major energy lift from Portland's second unit.
 Score: Lakers 27, Blazers 22 | 3:27 remaining in the first quarter 
 1 hour ago 11:31 PM Ziaire Williams Is Active
 Too late for him to score a sponsorship deal with that "Everything, Everywhere, All at Once" movie? He even has a behind-the-back dime already.
 Score: Lakers 22, Blazers 15 | 6:03 remaining in the first quarter 
 1 hour ago 11:27 PM He's Not a Walker
 Not to steal Walker Kessler's own joke here, but when he is running the floor at every opportunity and being rewarded when he does.
 1 hour ago 11:25 PM Speaking of Tough Covers
 What, exactly, is a defender supposed to against this? Sheesh.
 1 hour ago 11:23 PM Can't Give Lillard an Inch
 Ziaire Williams almost high-fived Damian Lillard at the top of this shot, and it was still too much space. What a player.
 1 hour ago 11:21 PM A Three, Some Free Throws and MVP Chants Already for Luka
 Adam Pantozzi/National Basketball Association via Getty Images 
 It's all offense, all the time so far. Or the exact scenario Luka Dončić was born to play.
 He hit an impossible-to-cover triple to start, then got his way to the foul line and was quickly serenaded with MVP chants—this time from his home fans.
 Score: Lakers 14, Blazers 7 | 8:27 remaining in the first quarter 
 1 hour ago 11:13 PM Three-Point Marksmen in the Building
 It's almost tip-off time, folks. Let the net-shredding commence!
 1 hour ago 10:58 PM Lillard Knows It'll Take a Clean Game Both Ways to Get the Win
 The Lakers, as Lillard put it, can absolutely "score a lot of points." In fact, these teams have the two most efficient offenses in the league so far, and no one is particularly close.
 L.A.'s league-best offensive rating is 125.9 points per 100 possessions. Portland's sits second at 123.5. The Houston Rockets have the No. 3 spot at 120.8, and no one else is at 119. Get that popcorn going, folks!
 1 hour ago 10:42 PM Scoot Henderson Is Available
 As good as Portland's starting guards have looked, the same can't be said for the bench backcourt. Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson are both holding sub-40 field-goal percentages, and the latter has gone an abysmal 1-of-9 from three.
 The Blazers would love to get Henderson, the No. 3 pick in 2023, some rhythm and comfort. And they'll get that chance, since he is available despite drawing an earlier questionable designations.
 1 hour ago 10:37 PM If It Ain't Broke...
 Same starters for the Blazers, because...Duh!
 Has Portland answered all of the logistical questions around the Dame-Ja backcourt? Not at all. But things are off to a promising start, and if this lineup manages to click, it puts a ton of talent on the floor and features impact players on both ends. Big test tonight, though.
 2 hours ago 10:32 PM Lillard Getting Loose
 We all remember Damian Lillard is 36 years old and returning from a torn Achilles, right? Because I think his stat sheet totally forgot.
 His volume looks a touch light, but only because Portland only needed 24 minutes out of him on opening night. Otherwise, this just looks like Dame: 22 points on 46.7/40/100 shooting with 4.0 assists against 1.5 turnovers.
 2 hours ago 10:23 PM The Rookie Wait Continues in L.A.
 It might be a little fuzzy after the sweeping roster changes in free agency, but before all that, the Lakers may have snagged a draft steal by acquiring swingman Cameron Carr with the 24th pick.
 The bouncy rookie plays a loud game—loads of athleticism, some fiery shooting runs—but L.A. fans haven't seen it yet. An oblique strain has delayed his regular-season debut, but it sounds like things are trending the right direction.
 2 hours ago 10:20 PM Measuring Stick Time for the Trail Blazers
 The Trail Blazers might be bringing an unblemished record into this tilt, but it features two wins over the Phoenix Suns (who were buried as soon as Portland opened the contest on a 21-0 run) and the Sacramento Kings (who were doomed during a disastrous third quarter).
 That's not to say Portland is anything other than good team, but it's worth noting this team hasn't played a good one for a minute. Even the preseason slate was soft: two games with the Golden State Warriors, one with those lowly Kings and one against the London Lions.
 The Blazers have a real chance to make a statement tonight, not to mention a chance to spotlight the latest leap from Toumani Camara. Already a highly regarded defender (sure to draw a marquee matchup here), his offensive output has erupted to 18.5 points on—wait for it—61.9/52.9/100 shooting.
 How much of this is remotely sustainable? We may be closer to finding out once this one gets rolling.
 2 hours ago 10:14 PM Luka Joins Lakers Legend in Historic Scoring Company
 A 52-piece on Sunday gave Luka Dončić more than the current scoring lead. It also tied him with Hall of Famer (and Lakers legend) Kareem Abdul-Jabbar for the 11th-most 50-point games in NBA history.
 Dončić won't turn 28 until February. He should have plenty of fire-breathers still ahead of him. Probably not enough to push Wilt Chamberlain for the top spot, but Dončić is far from finished moving up this list.
